text.p: The Belgian government on Tuesday unveiled its 1997 budget, which aims to cut the public deficit to 2.9 percent of GDP in 1997 from 3.3 percent in 1996 through an 80 billion franc austerity package.
Following are the main components of the package:
17 BILLION FRANC SPENDING CUTS IN FEDERAL BUDGET
of which
- 5.3 billion of cuts in subsidies for future pensions at the state-owned postal service.
- 5.8 billion franc savings on subsidies to state-owned companies via delay in payment
- 1.0 billion cut in international relations budget
- 1.0 billion cut in defence budget
23 BILLION FRANC SPENDING CUTS IN SOCIAL SECURITY BUDGET
- 19.6 billion of cuts in health care via measures, such as limits on spending on medication, limits on hospitalistion spending, limits on health sector wages
- 3.5 billion of cuts in unemployment and early retirement spending
23 BILLION FRANCS OF HIGHER TAXES
- 4.0 billion in new taxes on physical delivery of securities
- 1.2 billion in new taxes on savings book accounts
- 7.6 billion through closing tax loopholes for companies
- 7.3 billion from higher excise duties on petrol
- 3.9 billion from higher excise duties on beer and spirits
7 BILLION FRANCS OF HIGHER NEAR-TAX INCOME
- 4.0 billion from tax on company cars
- 1.9 billion from increase in social security charges for the self-employed
10 BILLION FRANCS FROM NON-FISCAL RECEIPTS, MISCELLANEOUS
of which
- 7.0 billion from sale of public buildings and land
